fullPassage: Several research studies have shown a strong correlation between social interaction and health and well-being. Yet there's not much social about kids retreating to their rooms to post selfies and comments to dozens or hundreds of followers they barely know in real life. Social media isn't very social. Since some children in elementary school are now being introduced to social media, they are becoming more anxious about how many people "liked" the photo they just posted or how many "friends" or "followers" they have online. It's hard enough for an adult to deal with disparaging comments online - or, conversely, a lack of comments, which we interpret as "no one is interested in me." Imagine how much harder it is for children. It's easy to say cruel things online because you don't see the effect of your words. It's one thing to post "No one likes you" and hit send from the comfort of your home. It's another thing to say the words "No one likes you" right to someone's face. We suggest you delay introducing social media to your son or daughter through adolescence. As your child grows into a teenager, she needs the firm foundation of being liked for who she is, by real people she knows. Online popularity is often based on performance, appearance, and shock value. This affection is conditional and misplaced. Your child needs to experience the unconditional love that comes from you. This love can prevent problems such as resentment, feelings of being disliked, guilt, fear, and insecurity. Remember, your child is asking the question, "Do you like me?" By limiting social media, you will help her find the answer in real people who care about her instead of an online society that can be fickle and cruel.

❌ ③ 일찍 익숙해지도록 권함 — 저자는 오히려 청소년기까지 도입을 미루라(delay)고 했어요.

questions.passage: Several research studies have shown a strong correlation between social interaction and health and well-being. Yet there's not much social about kids retreating to their rooms to post selfies and comments to dozens or hundreds of followers they barely know in real life. Social media isn't very social. Since some children in elementary school are now being introduced to social media, they are becoming more anxious about how many people "liked" the photo they just posted or how many "friends" or "followers" they have online. It's hard enough for an adult to deal with disparaging comments online - or, conversely, a lack of comments, which we interpret as "no one is interested in me." Imagine how much harder it is for children. It's easy to say cruel things online because you don't see the effect of your words. It's one thing to post "No one likes you" and hit send from the comfort of your home. It's another thing to say the words "No one likes you" right to someone's face. We suggest you delay introducing social media to your son or daughter through adolescence. As your child grows into a teenager, she needs the firm foundation of being liked for who she is, by real people she knows. Online popularity is often based on performance, appearance, and shock value. This affection is conditional and misplaced. Your child needs to experience the unconditional love that comes from you. This love can prevent problems such as resentment, feelings of being disliked, guilt, fear, and insecurity. Remember, your child is asking the question, "Do you like me?" By limiting social media, you will help her find the answer in real people who care about her instead of an online society that can be fickle and cruel.

다음 우리말에 맞도록 주어진 조건에 따라 영어로 쓰시오.

"그녀를 아끼는 실제 사람들 속에서"

[조건] (1) about, care, her, in, people, real, who를 모두 사용
       (2) 정확히 7단어로 쓸 것

det.korean: 그녀를 아끼는 실제 사람들 속에서
det.analysis:
'실제 사람들 속에서'는 「in + real people」로 시작해요.

→ 그 사람들을 꾸미는 관계절은 who care about her(그녀를 아끼는)로 붙여요. 사람 선행사라 주격 관계대명사 who를 써요.

→ 순서대로 이으면 'in real people who care about her'가 돼요. care about ~ = ~을 아끼다·신경 쓰다.
det.tip: in real people(실제 사람들 속에서) + who care about her(그녀를 아끼는). 주격 관계대명사 who로 연결해요.

questions.wa: in real people who care about her
accept: in real people who care about her

questions.passage: Since some children in elementary school are now being __________ (introduce) to social media, they are becoming more anxious about how many people "liked" the photo they just posted.
questions.stem:
다음 우리말 뜻이 되도록, 지문 빈칸에 괄호 안 단어 (introduce)의 알맞은 형태를 쓰시오.

일부 아이들이 지금 소셜 미디어에 소개되고 있기 때문에, 그들은 더 불안해지고 있다.

(영어로, 1단어)

det.korean: 괄호 안 introduce를 문맥·어법에 맞는 형태 introduced로 바꿔야 해요.
det.analysis:
'소개되고 있다'는 「be동사 + being + 과거분사」의 진행형 수동태예요.

→ are now being 다음에는 과거분사가 와야 하므로 introduce를 과거분사 introduced로 바꿔요.

→ 'are being introduced(소개되고 있는 중이다)'가 완성돼요. 주어(children)가 '소개받는' 대상이라 수동태를 써요.
det.tip: 진행형 수동태: be + being + 과거분사(introduced). 소개'되는' 것이라 수동이에요.

questions.passage: Several research studies have shown a strong correlation between social interaction and health and well-being. Yet there's not much social about kids retreating to their rooms to post selfies and comments to dozens or hundreds of followers they barely know in real life. Social media isn't very social. Since some children in elementary school are now being introduced to social media, they are becoming more anxious about how many people "liked" the photo they just posted or how many "friends" or "followers" they have online. It's hard enough for an adult to deal with disparaging comments online - or, conversely, a lack of comments, which we interpret as "no one is interested in me." Imagine how much harder it is for children. It's easy to say cruel things online because you don't see the effect of your words. It's one thing to post "No one likes you" and hit send from the comfort of your home. It's another thing to say the words "No one likes you" right to someone's face. We suggest you delay introducing social media to your son or daughter through adolescence. As your child grows into a teenager, she needs the firm foundation of being liked for who she is, by real people she knows. Online popularity is often based on performance, appearance, and shock value. This affection is conditional and misplaced. __________ that comes from you. This love can prevent problems such as resentment, feelings of being disliked, guilt, fear, and insecurity. Remember, your child is asking the question, "Do you like me?" By limiting social media, you will help her find the answer in real people who care about her instead of an online society that can be fickle and cruel.

det.analysis:
'~할 필요가 있다'는 「need + to부정사」로 나타내요.

→ 주어 your child(당신의 자녀)가 3인칭 단수라서 동사는 needs가 돼요.

det.tip: need + to부정사 = ~할 필요가 있다. 단수 주어(child)라 needs, 뒤에 to experience.

[ a / between / correlation / have / interaction / research / shown / social / strong / studies ]

det.korean: 연구들은 사회적 상호작용 사이의 강한 상관관계를 보여 주었다
det.analysis:
주어 + 현재완료 + 목적어 + 전치사구 순서로 배열해요.

→ 주어: research studies(연구들). → 동사: have shown(현재완료, 보여 주었다). 주어가 복수라 have를 써요.

→ 목적어: a strong correlation(강한 상관관계). → 전치사구: between social interaction(사회적 상호작용 사이의). 이어 붙이면 'research studies have shown a strong correlation between social interaction'이 돼요.
det.tip: 복수 주어(studies) + have shown(현재완료). a strong correlation between ~ = ~ 사이의 강한 상관관계.

questions.stem:
다음 우리말과 같은 뜻이 되도록 [조건]에 맞게 영어로 쓰시오.

"우리는 당신이 소셜 미디어 도입을 미룰 것을 제안한다"

[조건] (1) delay, introducing, media, social, suggest, we, you를 모두 사용

det.korean: 우리는 당신이 소셜 미디어 도입을 미룰 것을 제안한다.
det.analysis:
제안 동사 suggest는 뒤에 「(that) 주어 + (should) 동사원형」이 와요.

→ 주어 we(우리) + suggest(제안한다) + you(당신이) + 동사원형 delay(미루다).

→ delay는 동명사를 목적어로 받으므로 delay introducing(도입하기를 미루다)이 되고, 목적어 social media를 붙여 'we suggest you delay introducing social media'를 완성해요.
det.tip: 제안 동사 suggest + 주어 + 동사원형(delay). delay + 동명사(introducing)도 함께 기억해요.

questions.wa: we suggest you delay introducing social media
